To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

neural machine translation systems are better than traditional phrase-based statistical machine translation systems at interactive prediction, because neural machine translation models are better at predicting what a translator will write next.

• neural machine translation systems are well-suited for interactive translation prediction; • the neural approach to interactive translation prediction outperforms traditional approaches; • neural models provide better suggestions for rejected prefixes; • neural models can be efficiently adapted to the interactive translation setting.
• Neural interactive translation prediction is faster than statistical interactive translation prediction and yields higher prediction accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: • How to use a neural machine translation model to generate suggestions for the next word to complete the translation? • What are the advantages of using neural models over statistical ones for interactive translation prediction? • Can we efficiently compute the next suggestion in the neural model?
how to efficiently use a neural machine translation model for the task of interactive translation prediction.
how the encoder and decoder stages of a neural MT system can be adapted to the interactive translation prediction task.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neural machine translation is a very promising approach that has been shown to work very well for a variety of language directions.
neural machine translation systems can be used to produce better translation predictions than statistical machine translation systems.

the neural machine translation model is an end-to-end trainable model, which uses a bidirectional recurrent neural network to encode the input sentence and a recurrent neural network to decode the target sentence conditioned on both the input and the previous output words.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to show that neural machine translation systems are able to provide better translation prediction accuracy than statistical machine translation systems, while at the same time meeting the speed requirements of an interactive system.
we use neural machine translation models for interactive translation, which is a natural way to do it.
the encoder and attention mechanisms of the original model are used to produce suggestions, while the decoder is used to produce the final output.
The main takeaway from our work is that

neural machine translation systems can provide better translation predictions than traditional phrase-based systems, and that this is true even if the underlying machine translation system is the same.

we can use a neural machine translation model as a black-box for interactive translation prediction with only minor modifications, and that the resulting system performs better than the baseline system.
neural machine translation systems can provide better suggestions for interactive translation prediction than statistical systems, and that they can do this at a reasonable speed.
